terms.note: "Haredi" is the community's own term and is standard in Israeli English. "Ultra-Orthodox" is not a slur and is used by mainstream Israeli English outlets, but some Haredim feel it implies extremism; it is avoided for consistency only, and should not be treated as equivalent to the other terms in this list, which are pejorative. (Neutrality review 2026-10-06.)

Describes status without judging it. "Torato umanuto" is the Haredi framing and may appear only inside an option's own rationale. "Deserters" (עריקים) is a legal status for specific individuals, not a group descriptor.

Both sides' framings are loaded: "draft dodging" (opponents of exemptions) and "decree"/"persecution" (Haredi press). "Equal burden" (שוויון בנטל) is widely used but is one camp's slogan, so it appears only as a stated rationale inside an option.
The existing official framework name; used for the non-military alternative in both languages.
Standard in Israeli English and Hebrew.

Official Israeli administrative term and the term used by mainstream Hebrew media (e.g., ynet's 2026 election coverage); required by the PRD. "West Bank" is also common in Israeli English media and is not loaded, but is avoided for consistency with Hebrew. Some Arab and left-wing parties reject the term. Neutrality review (2026-10-06): to keep the issue recognisable and fair to those users, the judea-samaria moreInfo mentions once, in both languages, that the area is "also known as the West Bank" (הגדה המערבית). Everywhere else the PRD term is used.

English "settlements" is standard (PRD). In Hebrew, "יישובים" and "התיישבות" are the most neutral; "התנחלויות" is common and not offensive but slightly marked, so not used. "Outposts" (מאחזים) is a distinct legal category and should not be used for all settlements.

"Applying sovereignty" is the legal phrasing used in the Knesset bills and mainstream Hebrew; "annexation" (סיפוח) is also widely used in Israeli media, especially in English, and is preferred by critics. The legal act is the same; we use the bill's own wording. Neutrality review (2026-10-06): the judea-samaria moreInfo adds once "(also referred to as annexation)" / "(המכונה גם סיפוח)" so users who know the policy by that name recognise it; this is a symmetric "also known as", not a critics' label.
Neutral official name.
Described as a policy outcome, without characterization. "Separation" (היפרדות) is the mainstream Israeli term for disengagement-style approaches.

terms.en: the October 7 attack / the events of October 7
terms.note: "Massacre" (טבח) is accurate and mainstream in Israel and is not wrong to use; we prefer "attack" in neutral system text for consistent tone across languages and audiences. "Failures" (כשלים) is used because all major parties, including the governing coalition, acknowledge failures; "the debacle" (המחדל) carries an attribution of blame and is avoided as a label.

Legal term under the Commissions of Inquiry Law. Supporters call it 'independent' and some opponents call it 'one-sided'; both labels are avoided in neutral text and appear only inside option rationales.

terms.en: a commission appointed through the Knesset
terms.note: Opponents call the government's model 'political' or a 'cover-up'; supporters call it 'national' or 'balanced'. We describe the appointment mechanism factually instead.

"Reform" is the supporters' term; "coup"/"overhaul" are opponents' terms. A descriptive phrase is used; the specific measures (judicial selection, attorney general's authority, judicial review) are named directly.

terms.en: Supreme Court / High Court of Justice
terms.note: Official names. "High Court of Justice" refers to the Supreme Court sitting on petitions against the state.
Hebrew uses the feminine form when referring to the incumbent and the masculine generic form for the office in options. No personal names are used anywhere.

Used only inside the option of those who advocate it, in their own wording. It is also the official name of the Defense Ministry directorate approved by the security cabinet in March 2025 to facilitate departures from Gaza. Critics' terms are avoided because they would make the option unrecognisable to its supporters. Neutrality review (2026-10-06): kept, scoped to "Gaza residents", never used in neutral system text (titles, descriptions, moreInfo, questions).

terms.en: Arab society / Arab citizens / Arab communities
terms.he: החברה הערבית / אזרחים ערבים / היישובים הערביים
terms.note: "Arab society" (החברה הערבית) is the term used by government bodies, research institutes and Arab civil society today. "Sector" is considered dated and diminishing. "Palestinian citizens" is preferred by some but rejected by others, so it is not used.
